explanation: The electric potential a distance r from a point charge is V = kq/r, where k = 8.99e9 N·m²/C². Unlike the field, potential is a SCALAR: its sign follows the sign of q (positive charge → positive V, negative charge → negative V), and it falls off as 1/r (more gently than the 1/r² field). V is the work per unit charge needed to bring a test charge from infinity, where V = 0. On the AP exam this curve underlies energy problems (U = qV) and the relation E = −dV/dr; the animation sweeps a probe along r so you watch V climb steeply near the charge and flatten far away.
bullets: V is a scalar that falls off as 1/r — steep near the charge, flat far out.
Sign of V follows the sign of q (no direction, just magnitude and sign).
The dashed drop shows V at the probe's current distance r.
Reference V = 0 is at r → ∞; k = 8.99×10⁹ N·m²/C².
